question: At a posted or 85th-percentile speed of 60 mph, what advance placement distance does Table 2C-3 show for deceleration to an advisory speed of 30 mph?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a posted or 85th-percentile speed of 60 mph, Table 2C-3 shows an advance placement distance of 275 feet for Condition B deceleration to a 30 mph advisory speed. This is a guideline value that should be applied with engineering judgment, not a mandatory requirement. Guidance (recommended): - Table 2C-3's 60 mph row reads: "60 mph 1,100 ft 570 ft 350 ft 325 ft 275 ft 200 ft 100 ft6," where the values after the Condition A distance correspond to advisory speeds of 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 mph — giving 275 ft for the 30 mph advisory speed column. - "Warning signs should be placed so that they provide an adequate PRT," and "The distances contained in Table 2C-3 should be applied with engineering judgment"; the table's Condition B distances are adjusted for a sign legibility distance of 250 feet, and a minimum of 100 feet should be added for signs with less than 6-inch legend or more than four words. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 2C-3 shows, in the 60 mph row under the Condition B "30" advisory speed column, a value of 275 ft; [Image 3] shows the same Table 2C-3 in context on the Section 2C.04 page, confirming the 60 mph / 30 mph cell as 275 ft. Citations: - Table 2C-3 (p.152) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §804 (p.153) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §5 (p.152)
